title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Appropriate Equipment & Instrumentation - Biotechnology - Compound and inverted microscopes
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: A biomanufacturing facility uses an inverted phase-contrast microscope rather than a standard upright compound microscope in their mammalian cell culture suite. What is the primary functional advantage of the inverted microscope design for monitoring these specific cell cultures?
options: The objective lenses are situated below the stage, allowing the technician to easily view living cells clinging to the bottom of large, thick plastic culture flasks.
The light source is located beneath the stage, perfectly mimicking a dark-field environment without needing an annular ring.
It completely flips the image laterally, making it significantly easier for right-handed technicians to physically dissect tissues under the lens.
It physically shields the ocular eyepieces from intense biological cabinet airflow, preventing the lenses from drying out.
questions.explain:
Mammalian cells in culture typically grow as adherent monolayers, sinking to the very bottom of the liquid media and permanently attaching to the thick plastic floor of a cell culture flask (like a T-75). 

A standard upright microscope requires placing the glass slide very close to the objective lens on top, which is impossible with a tall, liquid-filled plastic flask. An **inverted microscope** places the light source on top and the **objective lenses underneath the stage**, allowing them to focus directly through the thin bottom of the culture flask onto the living cells attached there.

questions.q: Which of the following biological specimens would be most appropriately viewed using a standard upright compound light microscope rather than an inverted microscope or a dissecting stereomicroscope?
options: A thick, opaque sample of a whole leaf to visually examine its intact surface topography.
A living, confluent layer of CHO (Chinese Hamster Ovary) cells submerged under $20 \text{ mL}$ of liquid media in a plastic T-75 culture flask.
A chemically fixed and deeply stained section of mammalian liver tissue measuring only $10 \ \mu\text{m}$ thick, mounted flat on a glass slide.
A macroscopic, intact fruit fly being physically manipulated with fine forceps to sort male and female phenotypes.
questions.explain:
A **standard upright compound microscope** is designed specifically to transmit light up through a highly transparent, incredibly thin sample mounted on a flat glass slide (Option 'c'). 

> Option 'b' describes living cells in a thick plastic flask, which requires an *inverted* microscope (where objectives are below the stage). 
> Options 'a' and 'd' describe macroscopic, solid objects that require reflected light and lower magnification, which are best viewed with a *dissecting stereomicroscope*.
